summary: Episode Eleven returns after the imported-chip conflict with David Choe, Asa Akira, Yoshi Obayashi, Bobby Namba, and Critter. The opening constructs increasingly elaborate cuckold-film scenarios for Yoshi and Bobby, using Veruca James and Lexington Steele to test jealousy, acting, fantasy, race, and how participants imagine they would react to betrayal. That becomes a bridge into David's long account of meeting a Korean restaurant hostess while presenting himself as James, a Taiwanese contractor born in Korea. She gradually discloses that she strips and is a highly rated escort on The Erotic Review. David describes the relationship as affectionate, domestic, sexual, transactional, and built on reciprocal concealment: she does not know his public identity, while he studies her reviews and knows more about her work than he admits. Their eventual conflict moves through missed plans, Cheesecake Factory, gifts, silence, confession, anger, David's public-artist persona, a retaliatory bad review, and a later reconciliation that remains emotionally unequal. The panel uses the story to examine whether an escort or porn performer can be a partner, whether complete disclosure prevents harm, why apologies collapse into explanation, and whether leaving early is honesty or avoidance. Asa compares these dynamics with her marriage and her need for a partner she cannot dominate. David expands the argument into finite relationships, George Clooney and Derek Jeter as imagined masters of breaking up, a broken-infinity symbol, and his rejection of Romeo and Juliet and Titanic as evidence for lasting love. The episode closes with an attempt to arrange a listener date for Yoshi and Trivia With Bobby on adult performers and 2012 films.

connections.label: The false identity is an experiment that contaminates its own result
connections.note: David wants proof that he can be liked without fame or money, so he becomes James the contractor. Any affection he receives is then inseparable from deception: the experiment cannot establish ordinary love without denying the other person an informed choice.

connections.label: Both people disclose work while concealing identity
connections.note: She gradually tells David about stripping and escorting; David reveals pieces of his life while withholding his name and public career. Their intimacy grows through disclosure, but the information remains asymmetrical because he can read her reviews and social reputation while she cannot research him.

connections.label: Transaction and care coexist without becoming the same thing
connections.note: Cooking, companionship, sex, gifts, Korean conversation, and declarations of love occur outside a stated booking. The episode is most useful when it preserves that ambiguity rather than deciding that money invalidates affection or that affection erases the conditions of sex work.

connections.label: David's honesty solution repeats the same control problem
connections.note: After a relationship built on lies, David proposes telling future partners exactly when he will leave. Disclosure is more ethical than concealment, but the fixed three-month ending still lets him define the relationship's terms while hoping the other person will absorb the emotional cost.

connections.label: Leaving early is framed as harm reduction and avoidance
connections.note: David argues that departure prevents the deeper damage he causes by staying. Asa recognizes the selfishness and the hope that this time may differ. Both interpretations can be true: an avoidant exit may limit one harm while refusing the work of mutual repair.

connections.label: The chip argument becomes a relationship template
connections.note: Episode Ten's fight over intent, apology, and the word 'but' immediately resurfaces in romantic stories. The cast treats workplace conflict and marriage as structurally similar, while the archive must retain the different power and consent conditions in each.

connections.label: Titanic lasts because the relationship cannot continue
connections.note: David's critique is less about the film's craft than its promise: death freezes attraction before routine, class conflict, and incompatibility can test it. This connects his preference for finite relationships with his suspicion of romance made permanent by tragedy.

connections.label: The archive must not turn a vulnerable third party into an identified subject
connections.note: The escort story contains profession, ethnicity, workplace context, habits, and relationship details but no necessary public identity. Editorial value comes from the dynamics David describes, not from attempting to identify the woman.

quality.speaker_state: five-person panel with improvised role-play and interruptions; named turns withheld
quality.content_note: The episode contains explicit sexual material, pornography and cuckold fantasy, racist and homophobic slurs, threats of intimate-partner violence, sex work, deceptive identity, discussion of confidential reviews, bodily waste, relationship manipulation, retaliatory conduct, and unsupported cultural generalizations. The unnamed escort is not identified or treated as a public figure.
